🚨 Major Legal Victory for Tesla & Elon Musk! 🏆
Today, Vice Chancellor Bonnie W. David of the Delaware Court of Chancery dismissed multiple consolidated shareholder derivative lawsuits against Elon Musk and the Tesla board.
The cases — involving allegations around insider trading, the Twitter/X acquisition, and AI resource allocation — were tossed not on the merits, but because Tesla shareholders voted in 2024 to reincorporate in Texas and adopt a forum-selection bylaw requiring all derivative litigation to be filed exclusively in Texas courts.
Key excerpt from the ruling:

“I will not second-guess Tesla stockholders’ chosen forum by purporting to weigh the advantages and disadvantages of Texas law and procedure relative to our own… The owners of the corporation voted to require that derivative litigation be filed in a Texas forum. On the present facts, it is not inequitable to enforce their decision.”

This is a clear win for shareholder sovereignty. Tesla owners spoke, and the court honored their decision instead of allowing forum-shopping in Delaware.
Any refiled cases will now head to Texas business courts, which apply a more deferential business judgment rule — far friendlier to boards and executives.
Tesla’s move to Texas continues to pay dividends. Governance respected. Momentum building. 🚀

Big FSD news out of Europe!

The Dutch RDW has officially notified the European Commission that they’re going after EU-wide type approval for Tesla FSD Supervised, right after granting it nationally in the Netherlands.

Now it heads to a vote among member states — simple majority needed. The Netherlands has a strong history of setting the tone for the rest of Europe (and beyond).

They also dropped the full regulatory flowchart showing the exact next steps, plus how BMW and Ford already cleared their hands-free highway systems the same way.

Huge step forward! 🚀

“South Africa has openly racist ownership laws and is actively promoting white genocide.”

— Elon Musk, repeatedly calling out the South African government’s policies
South Africa is sliding deeper into institutionalized racism under the current government.

Instead of building a non-racial democracy after apartheid, the ANC and its allies have doubled down on race-based policies:

•  Expropriation Without Compensation — Laws allowing the seizure of land (mostly white-owned farms) without paying the owners.
•  B-BBEE racial quotas — Discriminatory rules in employment, ownership, and contracts that explicitly disadvantage non-Black citizens.
•  Farm attacks — Thousands of white farmers murdered since 1994, often with extreme brutality. The government downplays the racial motive while senior politicians chant “Kill the Boer.”
Elon Musk, who was born and raised in South Africa, has been one of the few high-profile voices calling this out for what it is: reverse racism that punishes competence and success based on skin color.
He has warned that South Africa is repeating the same mistakes Zimbabwe made under Mugabe — land seizures, economic collapse, and rising violence.
Instead of addressing crime, corruption, failing infrastructure, and economic decline, the government chooses to demonize successful citizens and push racial division.
Elon’s stance is simple: racism in any direction is wrong. A successful South Africa should be based on merit, rule of law, and unity — not resentment and redistribution by race.
The country had a historic chance after 1994. It’s now choosing the opposite path.
